exposure: Pre-existing maternal conditions (e.g. malnutrition, diabetes, obesity, severe anaemia, bacterial vaginosis, and group B streptococcus infections)
Unexpected or iatrogenic conditions during labour and childbirth, such as prolonged rupture of membranes (PROM) multiple vaginal examinations, manual removal of the placenta, and cesarean section
outcome: Maternal and fetal peripartum and postpartum infections
finding: The authors reviewed the literature on perinatal and postpartum infections and found that medical negligence may play a role in some cases of maternal and fetal infections, and that compliance with guidelines and best practices is crucial for preventing malpractice allegations and liability.
